chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about cupping for the fasting person, he said: Yes, if he does not fear weakness.

key_terms.حِجَامَة: Cupping (a therapeutic procedure involving suction on the skin)

ai.seo_question: Is cupping permissible for a fasting person in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that cupping does not inherently break the fast, distinguishing between the physical act and its physiological effect. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the fast remains valid unless the procedure leads to significant weakness or exhaustion, aligning with the broader legal maxim of avoiding harm (*la darar*). The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan scholarly tradition in preserving these practical rulings for daily worship.
